pairs.swarmLabel: Birds of prey lay few eggs, the kestrel excepted
pairs.singleLabel: Birds of prey are unprolific, except the kestrel

pairs.swarmLabel: Waterbird eggs have more yolk and less white than landbird eggs
pairs.singleLabel: Eggs of water birds have proportionally more yolk and less white

pairs.swarmLabel: Long pointed eggs hatch females, rounded eggs hatch males
pairs.singleLabel: Long pointed eggs are female and rounder eggs are male

pairs.swarmLabel: Hens and geese lay wind-eggs without ever copulating
pairs.singleLabel: Hens lay wind-eggs without ever having mated

pairs.swarmLabel: Egg and incubation periods in birds increase with body size
pairs.singleLabel: Egg and chick generation times scale with the size of the parent bird

pairs.swarmLabel: The heart is the first organ, a beating speck of blood
pairs.singleLabel: In the chick embryo the heart appears as a beating speck of blood

pairs.swarmLabel: The eagle usually rears two young and expels one from the nest
pairs.singleLabel: The eagle mother expels one of her two young from the nest

pairs.swarmLabel: The cuckoo builds no nest and lays in other birds' nests
pairs.singleLabel: The cuckoo lays in smaller birds' nests after eating their eggs

pairs.swarmLabel: Cartilaginous fishes are viviparous after internal eggs
pairs.singleLabel: Cartilaginous fishes are viviparous and all other fishes oviparous

pairs.swarmLabel: The smooth shark's embryo is nourished by a cord attached to the womb
pairs.singleLabel: The smooth shark's embryo is nourished by a navel-string like a quadruped's

pairs.swarmLabel: All cetaceans are viviparous, never carrying eggs
pairs.singleLabel: Cetaceans are viviparous

pairs.swarmLabel: All scaly fishes are oviparous
pairs.singleLabel: All scaly fishes are oviparous

pairs.swarmLabel: Only fish eggs sprinkled with milt after laying develop
pairs.singleLabel: Only eggs sprinkled by the male's milt produce young fishes

pairs.swarmLabel: The male sheat-fish guards the spawn for forty to fifty days
pairs.singleLabel: Only the sheat-fish guards its eggs, with the carp as a possible exception

pairs.swarmLabel: Some fishes arise spontaneously from mud and sand
pairs.singleLabel: Some fishes arise spontaneously from mud and sand

pairs.swarmLabel: Eels have no milt, spawn or reproductive passages
pairs.singleLabel: Eels do not pair or lay eggs and have never been found with milt or spawn

pairs.swarmLabel: Fish gestation always lasts a number of days divisible by seven
pairs.singleLabel: Fish gestation always lasts a number of days divisible by seven

pairs.swarmLabel: Viviparous selachians are less fecund but their young survive better
pairs.singleLabel: Cartilaginous fishes are less prolific than other fishes because they are viviparous

pairs.swarmLabel: Females are fiercest after giving birth, males in the rut
pairs.singleLabel: Females are most cross-tempered after parturition and males at pairing time

pairs.swarmLabel: Hybrid gestation follows the sire; the foal resembles the mother

pairs.singleLabel: Female mules may conceive but do not carry to term, except in Syrophoenicia

pairs.swarmLabel: Short gestation and fast growth argue against long deer lifespans
pairs.singleLabel: Deer are not long-lived because gestation is short and fawns grow fast

pairs.singleLabel: The newborn bear cub is smallest in proportion to its mother of any animal

pairs.swarmLabel: Hyenas are not hermaphrodites
pairs.singleLabel: Hyenas are not hermaphrodites and the female's false organ has no duct

pairs.swarmLabel: Hares breed year-round, superfoetate and bear every month

pairs.swarmLabel: Mice are the most prolific animals in litter size and frequency
pairs.singleLabel: A pregnant mouse shut in a jar produced over a hundred and twenty mice
